title: Vancouver Home Energy Rebates 2026: What Renters, Strata Owners and Homeowners Can Claim
desc: Vancouver rebates for 2026 from BC Hydro, FortisBC and CleanBC, including why windows are excluded in the City of Vancouver and what 45% ownership means.
badge: Heat pumps up to $4,000 for electric-heated houses
lead: Vancouver has 305,335 households, more than any other city we cover, and fewer than half of them own: 55% rent. Only 15% live in a detached house.
cards_heading: What you can claim in Vancouver in 2026
cards_intro: Amounts come from the program pages we re-read on October 2, 2026. Each card is a maximum, and most depend on how your home is heated.

cards.title: Whole-home heat pump
cards.note: Must replace electric heat such as baseboards or an electric furnace, meet 100% of the heating load at -5C and be installed by a Home Performance Contractor Network member.

cards.title: Partial heat pump
cards.note: For a heat pump that covers at least half of the heating load while replacing electric heat.

cards.title: Limited-time bonus
cards.note: Extra money on heat pump installs completed between August 1 and October 31, 2026.

cards.title: Income-qualified switch from gas, oil or propane
cards.note: CleanBC pays by income level (Level 3 / Level 2 / Level 1) for a central or three-head heat pump, for invoices from July 6, 2026.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: Attic, wall and basement or crawlspace work, paid per R-value added per square foot. Homes heated mainly by electricity only.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: $100 per opening, with a U-factor of 1.22 or lower.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Only when it replaces an electric water heater.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: $1,000 per kW, capped at half the cost, from an HPCN member installer.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: Up to $1,500 on its own with solar, or up to $5,000 with Peak Saver enrolment.

cards.title: EV charger
cards.note: 50% of a new wall-mounted Level 2 charger, plus $200 for a power-management device.

sections: The 2021 Census puts 43% of Vancouver households in homes built before 1981 and 45% as owners. Just 15% live in detached houses. There are 18,275 owner-occupied detached houses from before 1981, the largest pool among the 18 cities we cover. For those homes BC Hydro's rebates apply if the house is electric, and for the rest of the city the question is whether you own a strata unit, rent, or own a house on gas.
The window rebate is not available in the City of Vancouver

BC Hydro and FortisBC both exclude the City of Vancouver from their window and door rebates. Insulation, heat pump and heat pump water heater rebates still apply. If you are comparing Vancouver with Burnaby or Richmond, expect that difference.

Strata owners use BC Hydro's condo program, and the strata guide covers the amounts we verified. A tenant cannot claim a house rebate for a building they do not own, but low-income renters can ask about free upgrades. Of Vancouver households, 6.3% reported major repairs needed.
The January average low is 1.7°C, the record low in 2015 to 2024 was -14.1°C, and solar yields about 3.41 peak sun hours a day. A cold-climate heat pump rarely strains in this climate.

claim_steps: Work out if you own a house, own a strata unit or rent.
If you own an electric-heated house, price heat pump and insulation.
If you own a strata unit, start with the strata guide.
Skip the window rebate in the City of Vancouver.
faq: Why can't I claim windows in Vancouver?
BC Hydro and FortisBC exclude the City of Vancouver from the window and door rebate.
Yes. About 55% of households rent according to the 2021 Census.

18,275 owner-occupied detached houses were built before 1981.
Do apartments qualify for home rebates?
No. BC Hydro has a separate condo and apartment program.
